extracted.intended_audience: general readers, researchers, policymakers, and technical stakeholders interested in nuclear accidents and reactor safety
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted standards, design practices, and regulatory/operational failures and recommendations described in the Fukushima Daiichi accident article — covering reactor design, venting and filtration, backup power and generator protection, emergency planning, robotics, and oversight. Useful for informing nuclear-safety reviews, post-accident recommendations, and design assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtered Containment Venting Systems (FCVS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unpowered filtering systems on containment building vent lines (Filtered Containment Venting Systems) can safely catch radioactive materials and thereby allow reactor core depressurization, with steam and hydrogen venting with minimal radioactivity emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to reduce emissions during depressurization events; seen as a mitigation to allow controlled venting while limiting radioactive releases. Example: TEPCO later installed additional filters and vents. Anti-pattern: lack of filtered venting can increase uncontrolled releases during depressurization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtration using external water tank systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Filtration using an external water tank system is the most common established system in European countries, with the water tank positioned outside the containment building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design practice: place the water tank outside containment so it remains available after internal damage; external tanks can act as simple, passive filter/condensation systems for vented steam. Guidance implies preference for external, accessible filtration systems for containment venting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of hydrogen mitigation devices (avoid internal accumulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Had such devices been positioned at the top of the reactor buildings, where hydrogen gas collected, the explosions would not have occurred and the releases of radioactive isotopes may have been less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: hydrogen recombiners/vent filters should be located where hydrogen accumulates (e.g., top of reactor buildings) to prevent explosive buildup. Anti-pattern: placing hydrogen mitigation devices away from gas-collection points leading to ineffective mitigation and consequent explosions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Backup battery duration for Generation II reactors in flood/tsunami-prone areas
rubrics_metrics.description: For Generation II reactors located in flood or tsunami prone areas, a 3+ day supply of back-up batteries has become an informal industry standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design/operational standard: ensure off-site-power-loss scenarios can be managed for multiple days without external support. Scoring note: less than 3 days indicates insufficient preparedness for extended station-blackout events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hardened protection for backup diesel generator rooms
rubrics_metrics.description: Harden the location of back-up diesel generator rooms with water-tight, blast-resistant doors and heat sinks, similar to those used by nuclear submarines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical-protection criterion: generator rooms should be water-tight and blast-resistant and incorporate thermal dissipation measures so that flooding, blasts, or extreme environmental conditions do not disable emergency power. Anti-pattern: placing EDGs in easily floodable or otherwise exposed locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passive nuclear safety in reactor design (Generation III principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many constructed Generation III reactors adopt the principle of passive nuclear safety: they take advantage of convection and gravity to ensure an adequate supply of cooling water to handle the decay heat, without the use of pumps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design recommendation: favor passive safety features that function without power or active operator intervention. Assessment metric: the degree to which decay-heat removal relies on passive mechanisms vs. active powered systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robotics capability for high-radiation, degraded environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Robots lacked sufficient dexterity and robustness to perform critical tasks during the crisis; three widely employed robots became non-functional due to intense radioactivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational requirement: develop and field robots with high dexterity, robustness, and radiation tolerance for use in high-dose environments. Example action: DARPA-hosted competitions to accelerate humanoid robot development. Anti-pattern: deploying robots without adequate shielding/dexterity that cannot complete mission tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive risk assessment and collateral-damage planning
rubrics_metrics.description: The NAIIC found the causes of the accident had been foreseeable, and that TEPCO had failed to meet basic safety requirements such as risk assessment, preparing for containing collateral damage, and developing evacuation plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational/operational standard: perform proactive, comprehensive risk assessments addressing foreseeable hazards; prepare plans for containing collateral damage and for orderly evacuations. Scoring note: absence or inadequacy of such assessments is a major failure indicator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory independence and avoidance of conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The IAEA faulted lax oversight by the Japanese Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, saying the ministry faced an inherent conflict of interest as the government agency in charge of both regulating and promoting the nuclear power industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governance criterion: separate promotional and regulatory functions to ensure independent, stringent oversight. Anti-pattern: combined promotion-and-regulation agencies that may under-enforce safety to support industry interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act on updated tsunami and seismic hazard assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple studies (2000, 2002, 2008, etc.) warned of potential tsunami heights much larger than those assumed; TEPCO did not act on these findings and did not revise assumptions upwards or implement adequate protective measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safety requirement: incorporate the latest seismic and tsunami research into plant hazard assumptions and protective designs (e.g., seawalls, elevated critical equipment). Anti-pattern: ignoring internal or external studies that indicate higher hazard bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venting system design preference: passive over manually activated systems
rubrics_metrics.description: American nuclear scientists identified manually activated venting systems to be riskier than a passive approach. By 2011, new reactor designs used passive venting systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design criterion: prefer passive venting approaches that do not rely on timely manual activation under degraded conditions. Anti-pattern: reliance on manual vent activation that can be impossible during severe events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect emergency diesel generators (EDGs) from flooding and ingress
rubrics_metrics.description: Unit 1 EDG was disabled by flooding in 1991; later actions included installing doors to prevent water leaking into generator rooms. A TEPCO report detailed that the room was flooded through a door and cable holes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational design metric: ensure EDGs and their rooms are protected against water ingress (sealed doors, sealed cable penetrations, raised placement). Evidence of unprotected EDGs is a critical vulnerability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely collection and transparent use of radiation dispersion and fallout data
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances noted where radiation dispersion data were deleted or U.S. radiation maps were not used promptly; lack of use/transparency of radiation data hindered response and public information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crisis-management criterion: collect, retain, and transparently share dispersion and dose data with responders and the public; use available external data (e.g., allied measurements) promptly. Anti-pattern: withholding or deleting dispersion data and failing to consult external datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-accident health monitoring and assessment programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Various health-survey and monitoring programs (e.g., thyroid ultrasound examination program, Fukushima Health Management Survey) are cited to assess health consequences and guide relocation/evacuation measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public-health standard: implement systematic, long-term health monitoring programs after radiological incidents, including targeted screening and epidemiological studies; use findings to inform policy on evacuation, compensation, and healthcare.
